summary: Same 2D noise-field-through-a-3-colour-palette pattern with matching spatial scale and a complete 12-slider control surface, but the port animates ~3.0x too slowly, uses a 90-degree-spaced palette triad where the original uses 120 degrees, has a Motion slider that never changes its animation rate, and silently drops the stripe overlay whenever AutoColor is off.
observations: Both sides compile and run clean (no compileError/runtimeError), both report wantsSensors:true and were fed the beat120 synthetic sensor signal on every run. Default rig is grid 16x16 / 256 px.

STRUCTURE MATCHES. Both draw a 2D value-noise field mapped through a discrete 3-colour palette plus a dark/black level. Spatial autocorrelation measured on a 48x48 re-render along x: orig lag1 0.65, lag2 0.29, lag3 -0.06; port lag1 0.65, lag2 0.30, lag3 -0.05 — identical feature scale. Time-averaged column/row brightness profiles over a 100 s window are flat on both (orig cols 37-58, port cols 37-46), i.e. neither has a stuck bright/dark region.

SPEED: port is ~3.0x too slow. With AutoColor=0 (monotone fire palette, so luminance tracks the noise value), whole-frame Pearson correlation against t=0 crosses zero at t=0.108 s on the original and t=0.306 s on the port; the first correlation minimum is -0.84 at 0.20 s (orig) vs -0.80 at 0.60 s (port). Ratio 2.8-3.0x at every match point. `motion` avg at 20 fps baseline: orig 23.9, port 9.3 (untouched); orig 20.3, port 7.9 (AutoColor=0).

The slowdown is NOT frame-rate coupling. Rendering each side at 10/20/40 fps: orig motion 35/20/11, port 15/8/4 — per-frame motion halves as fps doubles on BOTH sides, and the decorrelation curves are identical in SECONDS across all three rates (orig 0.1 s -> 0.13/0.07/-0.01; port 0.1 s -> 0.86/0.85/0.85). Both sides are time-based; the port simply has a ~3x smaller time constant on its noise-field time term.

PALETTE GEOMETRY IS WRONG. The original always renders exactly three hues spaced 120 degrees apart, rotated by the palette dial: offset 0 -> 0/120/240, 0.15 -> 65/185/305, 0.3 -> 10/130/250, 0.5 -> 60/180/300, 0.7 -> 105/225/345, 0.85 -> 50/170/290. The port's three hues are 90 degrees apart at offset 0 (0/90/180) and irregular elsewhere (0.15 -> 50/140/230, 0.3 -> 105/195/285, 0.5 -> 0/180/265). Untouched defaults: orig hues ~96 (chartreuse) / ~216 (azure) / ~336 (rose), e.g. RGB (90,225,0), (0,51,129), (110,0,44); port hues 0 (red) / 90 (chartreuse) / 180 (cyan), e.g. RGB (248,0,0), (98,197,0), (0,80,80).

Port is also darker/greyer in the palette: at PaletteOffset=0, 24.4% of pixels are near-black on the port vs 17.6% on the original. Channel means at untouched default over 6 s: orig R/G/B 39.7/38.2/40.9 (balanced), port 44.3/54.1/26.0 (green-biased, blue-starved).

STRIPE OVERLAY IS DROPPED IN THE AutoColor=0 MODE ON THE PORT. With sliderAutoColor=0 and sliderNumberOfStripes swept over 0.05/0.3/0.6/0.92, the port produced FOUR BYTE-IDENTICAL renders (md5 d222d1..), identical to the no-stripes render; the original produced four distinct renders. Confirmed on brightness too: AutoColor=0 + StripeWeight=0.8 gives orig meanBrightness 17 (stripes cut ~half the light) and port 35 (unchanged from no stripes). With AutoColor left at its default (=on) the port's NumberOfStripes works normally, so the stripe layer is gated on the wrong condition.
Visually at AutoColor=0 + stripes the original overlays broad soft glowing bars that sweep across the noise; the port at the same settings is bare noise.

RESOLUTION BEHAVIOUR DIFFERS (invisible on the default rig). Re-rendered at --grid 48x48, the port's contact sheet is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its 16x16 render (md5 064dda00 both) — every 3x3 block is uniform (256/256 blocks), i.e. the port quantizes BOTH x and y to 16 steps. The original quantizes only x (100% of horizontally adjacent pixels inside a 3-block are equal, ~14.8 distinct colours per 48-px row) while y stays continuous (only 10% of vertically adjacent pixels equal, ~41.1 distinct colours per 48-px column). So the original gains real detail on a taller grid and the port does not.

STEADY STATE IS FINE ON BOTH. --skip 120 --seconds 12 --fps 20 reproduces the baseline exactly (orig mean 39 motion 24; port mean 42 motion 9); brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 1 (the unavoidable first frame). Nothing decays, freezes, or saturates.
Both sides are completely seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 render byte-identically on each side.

60 s / 10 fps and 240 s / 5 fps surveys show a single homogeneous regime on both sides — no mode rotation, no slow palette walk, no long-period beat. The only distinct 'regimes' are the ones the mode dials select (NoiseType 0/1, AutoColor 0/1, BassThreshold 0 vs >0), each of which was inspected separately.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: both sides expose 12 sliders and the probe calls all 24 responsive, but 5 names differ — orig sliderPerlinOrSimplex / sliderScale / sliderAutoColorPalette / sliderX_Offset / sliderY_Offset vs port sliderNoiseType / sliderZoom / sliderPaletteOffset / sliderXOffset / sliderYOffset.

BassThreshold semantics differ. On the original it is effectively binary: v=0 gives motion 23.9, and EVERY value from 0.02 to 1.0 gives a byte-identical render with motion 46.4 (measured over a 12 s / 20 fps window). On the port it is continuous: motion 9.5 at 0, 58.9 at 0.02-0.1, 39.2 at 0.5, 29.3 at 0.95-1.0.

In bass-reactive mode (BassThreshold=0.1) both sides show beat-locked horizontal banding in the rhythm image, but the motion-series autocorrelation combs differ: the original peaks at lags 4, 8, 19, 23, 27, 31 (dominant 4-frame / 0.20 s comb at 20 fps) while the port peaks at 9, 17-18, 26-27, 35-36 (~8.9-frame / 0.45 s comb).

dials.name: PerlinOrSimplex (orig sliderPerlinOrSimplex) / NoiseType (port sliderNoiseType)
dials.origEffect: Two-mode switch selecting the noise kernel; boundary is v > 0.5 (v=0.5 still renders mode 0). Modes are visibly different noise textures at the same scale.
dials.portEffect: Same two-mode switch, but the boundary is v >= 0.5 (v=0.5 already renders mode 1). Renamed from sliderPerlinOrSimplex.

dials.name: Scale (orig sliderScale) / Zoom (port sliderZoom)
dials.origEffect: Continuous; all 11 sweep values 0..1 render distinctly. Larger values give finer noise (spatial coherence measured on a 16x16 fire-palette render drops from 0.31 at v=0 to ~0.00 at v>=0.4).
dials.portEffect: Continuous and live in the same direction and roughly the same magnitude; all 11 values distinct. Renamed from sliderScale.

dials.name: Motion (sliderMotion)
dials.origEffect: Raises frame-to-frame motion from 20.3 (v=0) to 26.4 (v=1), and — more importantly — changes the temporal CHARACTER: at v=0 the field is periodic (self-correlation recovers to +0.79 at 0.4 s and keeps oscillating); at v>=0.25 it becomes non-repeating (correlation collapses to ~0 by 0.1 s and never recovers).
dials.portEffect: Reshuffles the field (all five sweep values render distinctly) but the animation rate is PINNED: motion avg 7.9-8.0 at v=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, and the self-correlation zero-crossing sits at 0.306-0.328 s at every setting. The port stays periodic at every Motion value (correlation recovers to +0.84 at 1.2 s even at v=1).

dials.name: AutoColor (sliderAutoColor)
dials.origEffect: Two-mode switch (palette-cycling colour vs a fixed monotone fire ramp); boundary v > 0.5. Mean brightness 33.6 in the fire mode vs 39.6 in the colour mode.
dials.portEffect: Same two modes but boundary v >= 0.5. ADDITIONALLY, turning it to 0 disables the port's stripe overlay entirely (see NumberOfStripes) — the original keeps its stripes in this mode.

dials.name: AutoColorPalette (orig sliderAutoColorPalette) / PaletteOffset (port sliderPaletteOffset)
dials.origEffect: Continuous palette rotation; all 21 sweep values distinct, v=0 and v=1 render identically (clean wrap). The three palette hues stay exactly 120 degrees apart at every offset.
dials.portEffect: Continuous, all 21 values distinct, v=0/v=1 also wrap cleanly — but the three hues are 90 degrees apart at offset 0 and irregularly spaced at other offsets. Renamed from sliderAutoColorPalette.

dials.name: NumberOfStripes (sliderNumberOfStripes)
dials.origEffect: Quantised into 5 levels with boundaries at exactly 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00 (i.e. floor(v*4)), verified with a 41-point hash-cluster sweep at 0.025 spacing. Higher levels move the column-profile DFT energy from k=1 to k=2/k=3 (more, narrower stripes). Works in every mode, including AutoColor=0.
dials.portEffect: Quantised into 6 levels with boundaries at 0.1667 / 0.3333 / 0.5000 / 0.6667 / 0.8333 (i.e. floor(v*6)) — so the same dial value picks a different stripe count over almost the whole range. Worse: with sliderAutoColor=0 the dial is completely inert (four sweep values byte-identical, and identical to the no-stripes render).

dials.name: StripeSpeed (sliderStripeSpeed)
dials.origEffect: Continuous; all 11 values distinct. v=0 freezes the stripe layer (NumberOfStripes then has no visible effect on either side).
dials.portEffect: Continuous, all 11 values distinct, and v=0 likewise freezes the stripes. Same character.

dials.name: StripeWeight (sliderStripeWeight)
dials.origEffect: Quantised into 5 levels via floor(v*4) (0.1-step sweep groups: [0,0.2],[0.3,0.4],[0.5,0.7],[0.8,0.9],[1.0]). Acts as an overall weight on the noise layer: meanBrightness 7 at v=0, 11 at 0.5, 34 at 1.0.
dials.portEffect: Same quantisation but the top level is missing — [0.8,0.9,1.0] all collapse to one level, giving 4 levels instead of 5. Brightness response is close but slightly brighter: 9 / 18 / 35 at v=0/0.5/1.0 vs orig 7 / 11 / 34.

dials.name: X_Offset (orig sliderX_Offset) / XOffset (port sliderXOffset)
dials.origEffect: Continuous pan of the noise field along x; all 11 values distinct, v=0 equals the untouched default.
dials.portEffect: Continuous, all 11 values distinct, v=0 equals its untouched default. Same character. Renamed.

dials.name: Y_Offset (orig sliderY_Offset) / YOffset (port sliderYOffset)
dials.origEffect: Continuous pan along y; all 11 values distinct, v=0 equals the untouched default.
dials.portEffect: Continuous, all 11 values distinct, v=0 equals its untouched default. Same character. Renamed.

dials.name: ShowProgress (sliderShowProgress)
dials.origEffect: Two-mode switch with a small effect (probe maxDelta 1.03) — a low-amplitude indicator overlay. Boundary v > 0.5.
dials.portEffect: Same small two-mode overlay (probe maxDelta 1.28) but boundary v >= 0.5.

dials.name: BassThreshold (sliderBassThreshold)
dials.origEffect: Effectively binary against the beat120 feed: v=0 leaves the pattern non-reactive (motion 23.9 over 12 s at 20 fps); every value from 0.02 to 1.0 gives an identical bass-reactive render with motion 46.4. Reaction shows a 4-frame (0.20 s) comb in the motion autocorrelation.
dials.portEffect: Continuous rather than binary: motion 9.5 at v=0, 58.9 at v=0.02-0.1, 39.2 at v=0.5, 29.3 at v=0.95-1.0. Its reaction comb is ~8.9 frames (0.45 s), not 4 frames. So the port both over-reacts at low thresholds and under-reacts at high ones relative to the original's flat 46.4.

feedback: Speed: the port's noise-field time term is ~3.0x too small. Measured on the fire-palette (AutoColor=0) render, the original's frame self-correlation crosses zero at 0.108 s and bottoms at -0.84 at 0.20 s; the port does the same at 0.306 s and 0.60 s. Multiply the port's time advance into the noise field by 3.0 and re-check that zero-crossing lands at ~0.11 s and that `motion` avg at 20 fps rises from 9.3 to ~24 at untouched defaults.

Palette: the original's three palette colours are always exactly 120 degrees apart in hue (a full RGB triad) and the palette dial rotates all three together — verified at offsets 0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85 giving 0/120/240, 65/185/305, 10/130/250, 60/180/300, 105/225/345, 50/170/290. The port produces 0/90/180 at offset 0 and irregular spacings elsewhere. Rebuild the palette as three evenly spaced hues (offset, offset+120, offset+240) rather than whatever 90-degree/4-stop table is in there now.

Palette phase at default: untouched, the original renders chartreuse (~96 deg) / azure (~216 deg) / rose (~336 deg); the port renders red (0) / chartreuse (90) / cyan (180). After fixing the 120-degree spacing, set the default offset so the triad lands near 96/216/336.

Palette darkness: the port leaves 24.4% of pixels near-black vs the original's 17.6% at PaletteOffset=0, and its channel balance at defaults is green-heavy (R/G/B 44/54/26 vs the original's balanced 40/38/41). Check the value/brightness curve applied to the noise value, not just the hues.

Stripes are gated on the wrong condition: with sliderAutoColor=0 the port drops the stripe overlay entirely (four NumberOfStripes values render byte-identically, and meanBrightness stays 35 where the original's falls 34 -> 17 at StripeWeight=0.8). The original draws its stripes in BOTH colour modes. Un-gate the stripe layer from AutoColor.

NumberOfStripes quantisation: the original snaps the slider with floor(v*4) — boundaries at exactly 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00, five distinct looks. The port uses floor(v*6) — boundaries at 0.1667 / 0.3333 / 0.5000 / 0.6667 / 0.8333, six distinct looks. Change the port to 5 levels with quarter boundaries; a 0.025-step hash sweep is the cheap regression check.
StripeWeight quantisation: the original has five levels (floor(v*4), v=1.0 being its own top level); the port merges [0.8,1.0] into one, so it only has four. Restore the fifth level.

Binary-mode boundaries are off by one hair on all three switch dials (NoiseType, AutoColor, ShowProgress): the original flips only for v > 0.5, the port flips at v >= 0.5. Only the exact value 0.5 is affected, but it is trivially fixable and it is the same off-by-one in three places.

Motion slider is functionally dead on the port: `motion` sits at 7.9-8.0 for v = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and the self-correlation zero-crossing never moves off 0.31 s. On the original the dial both speeds the field up (motion 20.3 -> 26.4) and, from v>=0.25, converts it from a repeating loop (correlation recovers to +0.79 at 0.4 s) into a non-repeating drift (correlation collapses to ~0 and stays). The port must gain that drift term.

BassThreshold: the original treats any non-zero value identically (all values 0.02..1.0 render byte-identically, motion 46.4) — it is an on/off enable, not a level. The port scales its reaction with the value (motion 58.9 -> 29.3 across 0.02 -> 1.0). Also the port's bass reaction cycles at ~0.45 s where the original's cycles at ~0.20 s.

Control names: rename the port's sliders to match the original exactly — sliderNoiseType -> sliderPerlinOrSimplex, sliderZoom -> sliderScale, sliderPaletteOffset -> sliderAutoColorPalette, sliderXOffset -> sliderX_Offset, sliderYOffset -> sliderY_Offset. The other seven already match.

Resolution: the port quantizes the y coordinate to 16 steps (its --grid 48x48 render is byte-identical to its 16x16 render, every 3x3 block uniform), while the original's y is continuous with the rig height. Invisible on the default 16x16 grid but wrong on any taller panel — sample the noise at the real y, not a 16-step index.

No regression needed on: spatial feature scale (identical autocorrelation out to lag 3 at 48x48), steady-state stability (both flat at t=120 s), seed independence (both byte-identical across seeds 1/7/1234), fps independence (both time-based at 10/20/40 fps), and the Scale/Zoom, StripeSpeed and X/Y offset dials (continuous and matching on both sides).
experiments: pq-0, pq-0.15, pq-0.3, pq-0.5, pq-0.7, pq-0.85 (palette hue-triple dumps)
nsA-0 .. nsA-1 (41-point NumberOfStripes boundary sweep at 0.025 spacing)
